article.headline: Washington takes on Toronto on 8-game skid

article.title: Washington takes on Toronto on 8-game skid
article.linkText: Washington takes on Toronto on 8-game skid
article.story: Washington Wizards (4-11, 12th in the Eastern Conference) vs. Toronto Raptors (5-9, ninth in the Eastern Conference) Toronto; Wednesday, 7:30 p.m. EST LINE: Raptors -7.5; over/under is 227.5 BOTTOM LINE: Washington aims to break its eight-game losing streak with a win against Toronto. The Raptors have gone 4-5 against Eastern Conference teams. Toronto ranks last in the Eastern Conference recording just 40.6 rebounds per game led by Scottie Barnes averaging 7.4. The Wizards are 4-8 in Eastern Conference play. Washington is 2-8 in games decided by 10 points or more. The Raptors are shooting 45.6% from the field this season, 1.1 percentage points lower than the 46.7% the Wizards allow to opponents. The Wizards average 10.3 made 3-pointers per game this season, 2.3 fewer made shots on average than the 12.6 per game the Raptors give up. The teams square off for the second time this season. The Raptors won the last meeting 112-102 on Oct. 23. Barnes scored 28 points to help lead the Raptors to the victory. TOP PERFORMERS: RJ Barrett is averaging 20.9 points, 6.4 rebounds and 4.3 assists for the Raptors. Barnes is averaging 15.9 points over the last 10 games. Trae Young is averaging 17.9 points and 8.9 assists for the Wizards. Anthony Davis is averaging 21.0 points over the last 10 games. LAST 10 GAMES: Raptors: 2-8, averaging 111.1 points, 38.5 rebounds, 28.2 assists, 8.1 steals and 4.1 blocks per game while shooting 46.2% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 116.7 points per game. Wizards: 2-8, averaging 110.1 points, 42.6 rebounds, 23.0 assists, 7.9 steals and 5.5 blocks per game while shooting 44.7% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 120.9 points. INJURIES: Raptors: Kawhi Leonard: out (knee), Nate Bittle: out (foot). Wizards: Tristan Vukcevic: out (hip), Jamir Watkins: out for season (acl), Justin Champagnie: out (foot), Reece Beekman: out (shoulder). ------ The Associated Press created this story using technology provided by Data Skrive and data from Sportradar.
